howToUse: canonicalText is the exact byte sequence the signature covers. Diff your own canonical builder against it first; every other failure is downstream of it.
canonicalBytesHex is the same bytes hex-encoded, for clients that would rather compare bytes than strings.
canonicalSha256Hex is what gets fed to ECDSA. Sign or verify THAT, never the JSON text.
envelopeJSON is the licence exactly as a verifier receives it, signature included.

Every vector is consumed the same way: canonicalise `claims`, diff against `canonicalText`, verify `envelopeJSON`. No per-case special casing, including the tampered ones — `mutate` records how a case was built, it is not an instruction.
Read canonicalText first. Every other disagreement is downstream of it.

PublicKeySpkiDerBase64 under testKey is exactly the string the client embeds as its compile-time constant: base64 of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, which is what .NET's ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo expects.
Each vector's expect.verify is what the reference implementation returns. 'fail' vectors carry the reason string verbatim.
verifySubject / verifyNowUnix / verifySkewSeconds are the inputs Verify was called with. A negative case means nothing without them — 'expired' is only expired relative to a clock.

Regenerating rewrites every signature (ECDSA picks a random k each time) and leaves canonicalText untouched. That asymmetry is deliberate: the canonical form is the contract, the signature is an instance of it.

algorithm.signatureFormat: IeeeP1363 fixed-field: r||s, 64 bytes, big-endian, then base64 std encoding
algorithm.publicKeyFormat: SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) DER, then base64 std encoding
algorithm.warning: `openssl dgst -sign` emits a DER signature, not IeeeP1363. Handing one to a fixed-field verifier throws a CryptographicException that points at nothing useful. See the der-signature vector.

vectors.name: buyout-perpetual
vectors.why: The product as it ships: a perpetual licence with no validity window and one entitlement. If this case disagrees, every paid user is broken.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.note: nbf and exp are both absent. Both canonical lines carry the '-' sentinel so the line count stays at 8.

vectors.name: entitlement-normalisation
vectors.why: Server code hands back entitlement lists in whatever order a map or an unordered SELECT produced. Unsorted, lowercase, padded and duplicated input must canonicalise to the same bytes as the clean form.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=OBSIDIAN-SYNC,PDF-DEEP-PARSE,PRO

expect.note: Trims, upper-cases, de-duplicates, then sorts by byte order. The input list order is irrelevant and must not survive into the signature.

vectors.name: entitlement-order-does-not-matter
vectors.why: The same entitlement set in a different input order must produce byte-identical canonical text. Two servers that build the list differently would otherwise sign different bytes for the same licence.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=OBSIDIAN-SYNC,PDF-DEEP-PARSE,PRO

expect.note: Compare canonicalText here against entitlement-normalisation: the two are byte-identical, entitlement line included. That vector's input is padded, mixed-case and duplicated, this one's is a different order — normalisation absorbs all of it, so none of it survives into the signed bytes. Identical text, not merely matching lines.

vectors.name: subscription-windowed
vectors.why: The windowed shape. Both timestamps present, so both canonical lines carry real numbers and the '-' sentinel goes unused.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=u9Kp4Zn8XvC2mLbTqR7hY0wS3dF6gH0a
plan=subscription
iat=1767225600
nbf=1767225600
exp=1798761600
ent=CLOUD-PARSE,PRO

expect.note: Unix seconds, no milliseconds, no timezone suffix. Skew is 300s on both edges of the window.

vectors.name: no-entitlement
vectors.why: A licence with no entitlement is rejected. The ent line still occupies its slot with '-', so the line count is unchanged.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=-

expect.note: Signature is valid over this payload; the rejection is a policy check, not a crypto failure. A client that verifies the signature first and then checks entitlements will report this differently — that is fine.

vectors.name: entitlement-blank-strings-only
vectors.why: Whitespace-only entitlement strings normalise to the same absent form as an empty list.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=-

expect.note: canonicalText should be byte-identical to no-entitlement.

vectors.name: tampered-plan
vectors.why: Someone edits the licence file and upgrades their own plan. The signature covers plan, so this must fail.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=subscription
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.note: Mutate the envelope after signing. canonicalText is the mutated text, so a client that rebuilds canonical form from claims will see the same disagreement here.

vectors.name: tampered-entitlement-added
vectors.why: The classic upgrade attack: keep a valid signature and append an entitlement to the list.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=CLOUD-PARSE,PRO

expect.note: The ent line is part of the signed payload. Adding to it after signing is exactly what the signature is there to catch.

vectors.name: tampered-subject
vectors.why: The licence is lifted onto another machine. The subject no longer matches the local installId.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=tR2pWq9LmX4kYbN7vHc0sJdE3uF8gH1a
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: licence belongs to another machine
expect.note: Fails at the signature as well as at the binding check. The subject is signed, so this cannot be made to pass by editing alone.

vectors.name: der-signature
vectors.why: The single most likely server-side mistake, pinned as a case: openssl emits a DER ECDSA signature and a fixed-field verifier needs 64 raw bytes. The failure looks like nothing at all unless you catch it here.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: signature is 70 bytes, want 64 (IeeeP1363; a DER signature is the usual cause)
expect.note: The reason string names the length and says a DER signature is the usual cause. If your client throws an opaque crypto exception instead, it has not reproduced this check.

vectors.name: signature-not-base64
vectors.why: A signature that is not base64 at all — a hand-edited file, a truncated copy.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: signature is not base64: illegal base64 data at input byte 3
expect.note: Decoding happens before length is checked, so this fails earlier than der-signature does.

vectors.name: expired
vectors.why: A windowed licence checked after it lapsed.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=u9Kp4Zn8XvC2mLbTqR7hY0wS3dF6gH0a
plan=subscription
iat=1767225600
nbf=1767225600
exp=1798761600
ent=PRO

expect.note: Expiry is inclusive at the boundary: now-skew >= exp rejects.

vectors.name: not-yet-valid
vectors.why: A windowed licence checked before its not-before.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=u9Kp4Zn8XvC2mLbTqR7hY0wS3dF6gH0a
plan=subscription
iat=1767225600
nbf=1767225600
exp=1798761600
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: licence is not valid yet
expect.note: Not-before is exclusive: now+skew < nbf rejects.

vectors.name: wrong-local-subject
vectors.why: A structurally perfect licence presented to the wrong machine. Signature verifies; the binding check is what refuses it.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=1
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: licence belongs to another machine
expect.note: No mutation: the payload and signature are intact. Only the local subject differs, which is what the second defence layer is for.

vectors.name: unsupported-version
vectors.why: A future format version must be refused rather than parsed on a guess.
vectors.canonicalText:
wechatbridge.license.v1
v=2
sub=kR7dQm2ZpX9vLbTn4HsYc1WjE6uF0aA3G
plan=buyout
iat=1767225600
nbf=-
exp=-
ent=PRO

expect.reason: license: format v2 is not supported by this client
expect.note: Signed at v1, then the version is bumped to v2. The issuer refuses to produce this at all — Issue rejects an unknown version — so the only way to build the case is to sign first and mutate after. That is also the shape of the attack it pins: a file edited on disk, not one the server produced.
